name: National Security Agency

profile.address: West Military Drive, San Antonio, Bexar County, Texas, 78245
profile.reading:
NSA Texas, formally the Texas Cryptologic Center, is one of the National Security Agency's cryptologic centers in the United States, alongside the agency's Fort Meade, Maryland headquarters and the Utah Data Center at Camp Williams. The San Antonio facility sits on the Medina Annex of what is now Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland and occupies a building with an unusual origin, a semiconductor fabrication plant Sony built and then closed in 2003. The NSA selected the shuttered Sony plant for its own use in 2005, a point at which the project was still discussed relatively openly in local reporting, and filed its first building permits with the city in May 2006 before the program's profile receded from public view.

Reporting based on a 2006 municipal bond document put the projected investment in converting and expanding the site at up to 300 million dollars. The building grew substantially during that buildout, from roughly 498,000 square feet across two connected structures to approximately 633,000 square feet, an expansion that included a dedicated 94,000 square foot data storage complex completed in June 2010. The facility became fully operational in late 2012. Bexar County property records tracked the site's assessed value rising from about 33.5 million dollars in 2008 to more than 72 million dollars as the buildout progressed, and the lease rate reported for the property, 34.69 dollars per square foot, ran well above San Antonio's citywide average of roughly 21.52 dollars at the time.

The project was projected to bring around 1,500 new jobs to San Antonio, on top of an estimated 2,000 military personnel and civilians the NSA relocated to the area from Lackland facilities as the program stood up in 2005. Consistent with the agency's practice for its cryptologic centers, the facility's funding does not appear as a line item in the Department of Defense's unclassified budget, and independent reviews of federal budget documents from 2004 through 2013 were unable to identify its funding source. As a signals intelligence and cyberwarfare facility, the Texas Cryptologic Center publishes no capacity, tenancy, or commercial specifications of the kind a colocation data center would, because it is not a commercial facility, and its technical specifications are classified rather than simply undisclosed. The clearest public record of the site therefore consists of property and permitting records, contemporaneous local press coverage of its construction, and a single, unrelated 2010 news item in which nearby residents reported that an NSA antenna was interfering with their garage door openers, a small but concrete data point confirming active signals equipment on site at that time.

reading:
The National Security Agency is a United States Department of Defense combat support agency responsible for signals intelligence and for the security of national security systems. It is in this registry because a large computing site it operates in Texas is mapped as a data centre, and the entry exists to record what is genuinely in the public domain about it and to be explicit about the very large share that is not.

The facility is NSA Texas, formally the Texas Cryptologic Center, on the Medina Annex of what is now Joint Base San Antonio in Bexar County. The site began as the Medina Regional Security Operations Center. In 2005 the agency selected a shuttered Sony semiconductor fabrication plant near the annex, closed in 2003, as the vehicle for a major expansion, and filed its first building permits with the city in May 2006, after which the project's public profile receded. Reporting drawing on a 2006 municipal bond document and on Bexar County property records put the projected investment in converting and expanding the plant at up to 300 million dollars, and traced the building from roughly 498,000 square feet across two connected structures to about 633,000 square feet after renovation, including a dedicated data storage complex of 94,000 square feet completed in June 2010. The same records showed assessed value rising from about 33.5 million dollars in 2008 to more than 72 million as the work progressed, against a reported lease rate of 34.69 dollars per square foot at a time when the San Antonio average was near 21.52 dollars. Around 1,500 new jobs were projected, on top of roughly 2,000 military and civilian personnel relocated to the area as the programme stood up in 2005, and the site became fully operational in late 2012.

The choice of building is not incidental and is worth understanding, because it recurs. A semiconductor fabrication plant already carries the heavy electrical service, chilled water plant, conditioned power and slab on grade construction that a large computing hall needs, along with the floor loading and the clean room shell. Disused fabs are converted to data centres repeatedly for that reason, and a conversion of this kind can be brought into service far faster and with far less new utility work than a greenfield build.

None of the four power figures this registry tracks is available for the site, and none will be. There is no published IT load, no utility service size, no standby generator count or rating and no on site generation figure. Reporting has noted that the facility's funding did not appear as an unclassified Department of Defense budget line item across the years of its construction, and the agency's own public materials acknowledge four cryptologic centres in the United States without publishing any facility detail for any of them. This registry records only what is already public and estimates nothing, and readers should treat any megawatt figure attributed to this site elsewhere as invented.

Two registry side notes apply. The stored street value is a reverse geocode to West Military Drive, which is a nearest road answer for a large military annex rather than a postal address, and should not be read as a building location. The agency has also historically occupied a leased satellite building near Loop 410 and Military Drive in addition to the annex itself, which is not separately recorded here, so this single row stands for a site rather than for a single structure.
